newsitem.title: USA: Palm Beach Cty, Fla., default is state's largest.
newsitem.headline: Palm Beach Cty, Fla., default is state's largest.

text.p: The default of $128.5 million Palm Beach County industrial development bonds is the largest muncipal bond default ever in Florida, said Patrick Smith, managing editor of the Defaulted Bonds Newsletter.
The default also ranks among the top 10 municipal bond defaults nationally, Smith said Monday.

The owners of the Osceola Power Limited Partnership said they would not make a $4.6 million debt service payment due on Tuesday, allowing two series of Palm Beach County industrial development revenue bonds to default.
The move had been widely expected since the partnership filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy reorganization in May.
"Everybody knew they weren't going to make the payment. That's why they filed for bankruptcy, so they wouldn't have to make the payment," Smith said.

The industrial development bonds that will default are $120.5 million of Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, tax-exempt series 1994 A, and $8 million of Osceola Power Limited Partnership Project, taxable Series 1994 B.
The owenrs have not decided whether to make an Aug. 15 debt service payment on another $160 million Palm Beach County bond issue that financed a second cogeneration plant.
The plants produce electricity by burning waste matter from sugarcane processing.
Palm Beach County Debt Service Manager John Long said the county had encouraged the plant owners to make the payment from debt service reserves. They have declined to do that, for now.

The county has no liablity toward the bonds, he said. "We've made it pretty clear to everybody, and we've even voluntarily reported to the NRMSRS, that we're not responsible for the debt service payment or the bonds."
